title: Boot a personal PS2 homebrew ELF from PCSX2
summary: Use the documented `-elf` override to test a lawful homebrew executable separately from a disc image and ordinary library launch.
heroAlt: A PlayStation 2 console with its controller and accessories on a light background.
author: EmuCore - Hub
searchKeywords: boot a personal ps2 homebrew elf in pcsx2
Boot a personal PS2 homebrew ELF from PCSX2

blocks.text: PCSX2’s command-line reference describes `-elf <file>` as overriding the boot ELF with the specified filename. This supports testing a homebrew executable directly when you are developing it or have lawful access to it. It does not convert a disc image, supply system firmware, or establish that arbitrary executable files are trustworthy.

Use an ELF you built yourself or obtained from a project that explicitly permits its distribution. Keep it separate from commercial game files. Confirm PCSX2 already starts normally with your own BIOS dump, and back up any active development build. Do not run unknown binaries from file-sharing bundles.

items: 1. Record the path to the PCSX2 executable and the test ELF.
2. Copy your normal launch shortcut and keep its data-folder arguments unchanged.
3. Add `-elf` followed by the full ELF file path to the copied command.
4. Do not also pass a game image unless you are intentionally testing the documented override behavior.
5. Start PCSX2 and observe the homebrew’s startup screen or known test result.
6. Close PCSX2, inspect its log if startup fails, and rerun the same ELF once after verifying its path.

blocks.text: Pass when PCSX2 reaches the expected homebrew output and the ordinary library launch still works afterward. A black screen alone does not prove the emulator is broken: the ELF may target different hardware, require unavailable peripherals, or fail before drawing output. Compare against the homebrew project’s own requirements.

items: File not found: verify the exact ELF path and shell quoting.
BIOS error: confirm the emulator uses your own configured firmware.
Homebrew shows no screen: check its target, dependencies, and compatibility notes with its authors.
Ordinary shortcut boots the test instead: remove `-elf` from the normal launcher.

blocks.text: Close PCSX2 and remove the override from the copied command. Return to the normal library shortcut. Delete the test ELF only if you no longer need it; do not modify or replace BIOS, game images, or memory-card data to troubleshoot the override.
